themes_detail.label: Food Safety Spike This Week
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints in CD 408 surged to 7 THIS WEEK—a 300% spike from the 1.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.42)—signaling either a sudden cluster of violations or a shift in resident reporting of food safety issues.
evidence: 7 food establishment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly average (z-score: 5.42, 300% spike)
No prior news mentions or community board discussion of food safety emergencies
Timing suggests acute event or pattern rather than chronic problem
reporting_angles: Are specific restaurants or food vendors involved? What violations were cited?
Is there a seasonal or event-driven explanation (holiday catering, reopening, inspection blitz)?

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Complaints Jump
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints in CD 408 jumped to 5 LAST WEEK—a 1,900% spike from the 0.2 weekly baseline over 8 weeks (z-score: 7.18)—suggesting either newly discovered contamination in buildings or a compliance/demolition event triggering exposure concerns.
evidence: 5 asbestos complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 7.18, 1,900% spike)
647 DOB permit filings in last 90 days (381 alterations, 17 full demolitions) suggest active construction/renovation work that may disturb asbestos
Community Board has standing request for additional building inspectors, implying inspection capacity gaps
reporting_angles: Which buildings or demolition sites triggered the complaints? Are they near schools or residences?
Is the DOB tracking asbestos abatement compliance during renovations and demolitions?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Fireworks Crisis (Declining)
themes_detail.summary: Illegal fireworks complaints peaked at 32 TWO WEEKS AGO—a stunning 12,700% spike from the 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 48.0)—but the recency of that spike is fading; this warrants investigation into what triggered the event and whether the threat has subsided.
evidence: 32 fireworks complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 48.0, 12,700% spike—highest z-score in dataset)
No current data on whether complaints have returned to baseline or remain elevated
No Reddit discussions or local news coverage explaining the spike
reporting_angles: Was there a specific event (holiday, protest, gathering) that triggered the surge?
Has the NYPD conducted enforcement? Have complaints tapered off or is illegal fireworks now a sustained problem?

themes_detail.label: Residential Waste Disposal Surge
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints in CD 408 jumped to 6 LAST WEEK—a 336% spike from the 1.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.16)—suggesting either new enforcement of waste rules or a localized problem with sanitation practices or pickup failures.
evidence: 6 residential disposal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (z-score: 4.16, 336% spike)
Community Board has standing request for catch basin cleaning (DEC), suggesting ongoing drainage/sanitation infrastructure concerns
Street conditions rank high in baseline complaints (1,440 over 90 days), indicating broader sanitation/infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Are specific neighborhoods or blocks affected? Is this a pickup schedule failure or illegal dumping?
Is the spike tied to the holidays or a change in sanitation policy enforcement?

themes_detail.label: Traffic Congestion Spike (Fading)
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints in CD 408 spiked to 81 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 248% surge from the 23.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.28)—but the age of the spike (2 weeks) and lack of current follow-up data make it unclear if this reflects a persistent problem or a temporary event.
evidence: 81 traffic complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 23.2 weekly average (z-score: 4.28, 248% spike)
Illegal parking (2,262 complaints over 90 days) and blocked driveway (942) complaints suggest chronic traffic issues
Five active ULURP applications (St. Francis Prep, 164th Street, Union Turnpike, Queens Boulevard rezoning) may drive future traffic demand
reporting_angles: Did a specific event (construction closure, school opening, special event) trigger the spike 2 weeks ago?
Are current traffic levels back to normal or sustained? Do pending rezonings risk worsening congestion?
